howto.name: Upload the PDF
howto.text: Select a PDF that contains one or more tables you need to extract as structured data.

howto.name: Extract the tables
howto.text: Click Extract Tables. Every page is checked with PyMuPDF table detection, which finds tables drawn with ruled lines; there is no page selection on this page.

howto.name: Check the CSV
howto.text: All detected tables go into one CSV file in page order, with a blank row between tables. Cells that start with =, +, - or @ get a leading apostrophe so spreadsheet apps do not run them as formulas; this includes negative numbers.

howto.name: Download the extracted data
howto.text: For one PDF, the CSV downloads automatically, named after your PDF. For several PDFs, download each CSV or all of them as one ZIP.

faq.a: CSV only. All detected tables go into one CSV file, with a blank row between tables. For an Excel workbook, use PDF to Excel, which puts each page on its own sheet.

faq.q: Can it extract tables from scanned PDFs?
faq.a: Usually not. Detection looks for ruled lines drawn in the PDF itself, and a scanned page is a picture, so no table is found even after the OCR tool adds a text layer. The tool works on digitally created PDFs whose tables have ruled borders.

faq.q: How does the tool detect table boundaries?
faq.a: It uses PyMuPDF table detection, which looks for the ruled lines drawn around and between cells. Tables laid out with spacing alone, without visible borders, are usually not detected, and when no table is found you get an error instead of a CSV.
